sections.h2: Where is Carpentersville and what is the village like?
sections.html:
Carpentersville is a village in northern Kane County, Illinois, on the Fox River and part of the Chicago metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 37,983 residents in 8.09 square miles, of which 7.88 are land.

The village runs under a council-manager form of government: an elected president and six trustees appoint a professional manager who runs daily operations. For a seller, the practical point is that Carpentersville handles its own permits, water billing and rental licensing, so most of the paperwork stays at Village Hall rather than moving to a county office.

  • County: Kane, with deeds recorded by the Kane County Recorder in Geneva
  • Green space: Carpenter Park, the Carpentersville Dam area and Raceway Woods Forest Preserve
  • Housing units in 2020: 11,777, of which 2.9 percent were vacant

sections.h2: How did the Fox River settlement become Carpentersville?
sections.html:
In 1837 the Carpenter brothers were heading for the Rock River when spring floods stopped their oxcart journey on the east bank of the Fox River. They stayed and called the place Carpenters' Grove. Julius Angelo Carpenter built the first store, bridge and factory, and he later served two terms in the Illinois House.

The Illinois Iron and Bolt foundry anchored early industry, and an electric interurban line reached the foundry in 1896. For about a hundred years the town grew slowly. Until the 1950s it was a street grid along the river centered on Main Street, which was the only highway bridge across the Fox between Algonquin and Dundee.

Then the suburbs arrived. The population went from 1,523 in 1950 to 17,424 in 1960, the fastest jump in the village's history. Older homes near the river and the post-1950 subdivisions are very different housing, and a seller should know which type they own when pricing.

sections.h2: How has the population changed since 1950?
sections.html:
The census counts show one great leap in the 1950s, a flat stretch through the 1980s and steady growth into the 2000s. Growth since 2010 has been small, up 0.8 percent between 2010 and 2020.

The 2020 median age was 32.5, and 29.6 percent of residents were under 18. Of 11,439 households, 47.8 percent had children at home. That is a young, family-heavy village, so house size and layout matter to the likely buyer pool.

sections.h2: What do the village's housing numbers say about demand?
sections.html:
The 2020 census recorded a homeowner vacancy rate of 0.9 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 5.0 percent. A homeowner vacancy rate that low suggests few for-sale houses sit empty, which is generally favorable to a seller who prices the house sensibly.

The village's income section lists a median household income of $73,105 and a median family income of $79,102, with a per capita income of $26,770. Those figures help frame what a buyer who needs a mortgage can afford, and they are one reason some owners prefer a cash buyer who does not depend on lender approval.

sections.h2: What landmarks and shopping areas shape the village?
sections.html:
The Meadowdale Shopping Center opened in May 1957 and had grown to as many as 53 stores a year later. A November 1963 fire destroyed 25 stores and an ice rink, and the mall reopened in November 1964 without the rink. A competing mall opened 2.5 miles west in 1980, and Meadowdale shrank through the 1980s. Part of it was demolished in 1989, and a Walmart opened on the east end in 2016.

From 1958 to 1969 the Meadowdale International Raceway, a 3.27 mile track west of Illinois Route 31, ran here. The site is now a township park and county forest preserve. Since the 1990s, growth has moved west along Randall Road, where newer subdivisions and shopping centers sit.

The Dundee Township Historic District appears among the village's related places. If your house is in the older river-side grid, ask Village Hall whether any local review applies before you plan exterior changes.

sections.h2: How do people get around Carpentersville?
sections.html:
Illinois Route 31 runs past the older river-side grid, and Randall Road is the corridor where the newer subdivisions and shopping centers were built. Pace buses connect the village to Crystal Lake, Elgin and other destinations. A Chicago and North Western line between Elgin and Crystal Lake served Carpentersville from 1904 to 1932.

A buyer comparing Carpentersville with its neighbors will look at bus access and drive times, so mention both in a listing.

sections.h2: Does Carpentersville charge a transfer stamp on a sale?
sections.html:
No. The village's transfer stamp page says Carpentersville does not have a transfer stamp requirement for real estate transactions. This puts it among the simpler closings for a seller in the northwest suburbs.

The seller still has one task. Call the Water Billing Department at 847-551-3476 to schedule a final reading on the water meter. The new owner then opens service in person at Village Hall with a settlement statement or deed, a completed water application and picture identification.

State tax still applies. Illinois taxes the transfer of title at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction thereof under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, based on the declaration filed for the sale.

sections.h2: What permits and inspections come up when selling in Carpentersville?
sections.html:
The Community Development Department issues permits for construction, and the village's permit page says even a new water heater or a shed needs some kind of permit or approval. It also links a list of work that does and does not need one.

  • Past work: if the previous owner added a deck, finished a basement or replaced a furnace, confirm the permit was closed
  • Open work: a buyer who takes the house as-is takes the open permit with it
  • Rental houses: the village runs a rental licensing program with an initial inspection and an annual license

The village's rental licensing checklist, last revised in 2011, describes a temporary certificate after an application, then an inspection, then a follow-up inspection if violations are found, and a Crime Free Housing seminar the owner must attend. Ask Community Development for the current version before you rely on it. If you plan to sell a tenant-occupied house, note that the owner is responsible for getting tenant consent for inspection visits.

sections.h2: Where is the deed recorded for a Carpentersville sale?
sections.html:
The Kane County Recorder in Geneva keeps the land records for the village. The recorder's website provides a records search, and the office describes services including recording, copying, scanning and a tract department.

The recorder has also announced a free Property Watch service aimed at deed fraud, which the office says targets homeowners at risk of foreclosure. An owner of a vacant or inherited house may want to look at it.

sections.h2: How do a regular listing and a cash sale compare in Carpentersville?
sections.html:
A listing makes sense when the house is move-in ready and you can wait out showings and a buyer's financing. A cash sale as-is makes sense when repairs, a tenant, an inherited estate or a deadline would make a listing slow or costly.

In either case the village side is light: no municipal stamp, a final water reading and the permit review above. That leaves the seller's time and repair costs as the real variables, so compare the net result of each route rather than the headline price.

faqs.q: Do I need a village transfer stamp to sell in Carpentersville?
faqs.a: No. The village states it has no transfer stamp requirement for real estate sales. You should still schedule a final water meter reading by calling Water Billing at 847-551-3476.

faqs.q: What does the buyer need to start water service?
faqs.a: The new owner brings a settlement statement or deed to Village Hall in person, fills out the water application and shows picture identification.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a water heater or shed in Carpentersville?
faqs.a: Yes, in general. The village's building page says work from a new water heater or shed up to a full building requires some type of permit or approval. Check the village's list of work that does and does not need a permit before you start.
Kane County. The Kane County Recorder in Geneva records deeds and offers an online records search.

faqs.q: How much did Carpentersville grow in the last census decade?
faqs.a: Slightly. The population rose from 37,691 in 2010 to 37,983 in 2020, a gain of 0.8 percent.
